title.value: Summarize a private repo's app flow with Copilot

introduction.value:
A developer asked Copilot to summarize an app's flow and component interactions on a client's private repo, then worried the session used their personal account.
·
Nov 19, 2026

method.value: The developer, added as an outside collaborator on a client’s private GitHub repo, used Copilot on github.com while logged into their own Copilot Free account. They asked it to summarize the app flow and component interactions, then posted because they realized afterward the session was tied to their personal account and they were worried about training, visibility to the client, and having used a phone hotspot to bypass a block.

outcome.value: There was no reported project outcome beyond getting the summary; the thread is mainly about the risk afterward. Comments pointed to possible exposure around policy and training settings, but the post does not report any actual leak, warning, or client response.

notes.value: The catch is account context: they only noticed after the fact that the repo access came from the client, but the Copilot session was still running under their personal Copilot Free account.

source_text.body:
Summarize a private repo's app flow with Copilot
A developer asked Copilot to summarize an app's flow and component interactions on a client's private repo, then worried the session used their personal account.
·
Nov 19, 2026
Done with
GH
GitHub Copilot
What they did
The developer, added as an outside collaborator on a client’s private GitHub repo, used Copilot on github.com while logged into their own Copilot Free account. They asked it to summarize the app flow and component interactions, then posted because they realized afterward the session was tied to their personal account and they were worried about training, visibility to the client, and having used a phone hotspot to bypass a block.
How it went
There was no reported project outcome beyond getting the summary; the thread is mainly about the risk afterward. Comments pointed to possible exposure around policy and training settings, but the post does not report any actual leak, warning, or client response.
Worth knowing
The catch is account context: they only noticed after the fact that the repo access came from the client, but the Copilot session was still running under their personal Copilot Free account.
Try it yourself
with
GitHub Copilot
Copy prompt
Read the repository at [path] and summarize how the app works: the entry points, main components, how they communicate, and the data flow. Finish with a simple diagram in text and a list of the five files I should read first. Don't modify anything in the repo.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/GithubCopilot/comments/1y0elui/used_my_personal_copilot_free_on_a_clients
